items.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
items.summary: It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years. Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

items.title: ‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival
items.summary: New head coach faces tough opening match at Anfield ‘It’s a big challenge but at the same time it’s adrenaline’ Mauricio Pochettino said it was “an honour” and “a privilege” to be the new Manchester United head coach after arriving in England on Wednesday. Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight after overseeing the USA beating Haiti in his final game in charge. Members of Pochettino’s staff landed earlier in the week to begin work at Carrington , laying the foundations as United seek to turn their season around.

items.title: Football Daily | From Cincinnati to Manchester: Pochettino in a hurry to paint town red
items.summary: With his team mired in the relegation zone and a massive match at Liverpool this weekend, Mauricio Pochettino has been understandably busy since being appointed head coach of Manchester United. Unfortunately for Old Trafford regulars, the small print of his contract meant the Argentinian was tied up masterminding victory for USA USA USA in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti when he ought to have been in Carrington moving red magnets around a tactics board in front of Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire.

items.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
items.summary: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA’s chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 44-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4bn) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game.

items.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
items.summary: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. He’s always asking what more we can do.” Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work.
